Full 100-topic benchmark deferred to a future authorised sprint. Every topic ships with: (a) an alias set for the deterministic classifier · (b) a canonical sub-question decomposition · (c) an evidence-taxonomy tag per sub-claim · (d) never-says list · (e) layer summary for the response composer. aliases: how did they build the pyramids
how were the egyptian pyramids constructed
were the pyramids built by slaves
were slaves used to build the pyramids

sub_claims.claim: Ancient Egyptians quarried and transported the stones
Skilled paid workers · not enslaved populations · did the construction
Some form of ramp system was used to raise blocks
Sophisticated surveying and mathematics were applied
Extraterrestrial beings built the pyramids
A prior lost advanced civilisation built the pyramids

topics.layer_summary: Established: Egyptians quarried and organised the labour. Disputed: exact ramp/lifting method. Speculative: alien or lost-civilisation authorship.
topics.discussion_opener: There are three questions inside this one: who was the workforce, what methods did they use, and what remains uncertain. The evidence sits differently on each.
topics.offer_to_expand: I can walk through the archaeological evidence on labour and surveying, then the disputed engineering questions, then the modern alternative hypotheses and how they compare.
never_says: aliens definitely did not build the pyramids
the pyramids were built by slaves

sub_claims.claim: Cultures across the world told stories about giants
Ancient peoples believed some giants were real
The Nephilim appear in Hebrew biblical texts
There is accepted archaeological evidence for a race of enormous humans

topics.layer_summary: Stories: yes, widely. Ancient belief: yes, in many traditions. Archaeological evidence for a race of enormous humans matching those stories: no accepted evidence.
topics.discussion_opener: There are three separate questions inside 'did giants exist' · the story tradition · what ancient people believed · and whether archaeology supports a population of enormous humans.
topics.offer_to_expand: I can walk through the major traditions (Greek, biblical, Norse, Native American) and the archaeological record separately.

sub_claims.claim: Plato wrote about Atlantis in Timaeus and Critias
Plato's intent (literal history vs allegory) is a scholarly debate
Atlantis was a real advanced civilisation that sank in the ocean
Various real locations (Thera/Santorini · Doggerland · others) have been proposed

topics.layer_summary: Ancient text: established. Real advanced civilisation: not established. Candidate real-world inspirations: actively discussed but not settled.
topics.discussion_opener: Atlantis is a good case study in separating story, ancient source, and modern claim.
topics.offer_to_expand: I can walk you through what Plato actually wrote, how the story travelled through later interpreters, and how the modern candidate-location theories compare.
never_says: Atlantis is just fiction and nothing more

aliases: did the anunnaki come to earth

sub_claims.claim: The Anunnaki are figures in ancient Mesopotamian religious tradition
The relevant Sumerian and Akkadian texts are well documented
The Anunnaki were extraterrestrial beings who visited Earth
The extraterrestrial interpretation was popularised in the 20th century

topics.layer_summary: Ancient religious figures: established. Ancient extraterrestrial visitation: not established by the surviving sources · that is a modern interpretation.
topics.discussion_opener: Two distinct things are worth separating: what the ancient Mesopotamian texts actually say about the Anunnaki, and how the modern ancient-astronaut interpretation of those texts developed.
topics.offer_to_expand: I can outline the primary Sumerian/Akkadian sources first, then how Sitchin and others in the 20th century reinterpreted them.
never_says: ancient Mesopotamians believed the Anunnaki were aliens

topics.display_name: The historicity of Jesus of Nazareth

sub_claims.claim: A historical person named Jesus of Nazareth existed in first-century Judea
Every detail in the Gospel accounts is historically established as fact
Jesus performed miracles
Jesus rose from the dead
Jesus is God · or the Son of God

topics.layer_summary: Most historians of antiquity regard Jesus as a historical person. Theological claims about miracles, resurrection and divinity belong to religious tradition · a different kind of evidence.
topics.discussion_opener: The historicity question and the theological questions require different kinds of evidence. It helps to separate them.
topics.offer_to_expand: I can outline the historical evidence for the person separately from the religious tradition around what he did and who he was.
never_says: the Gospels are complete historical records
the resurrection is a matter of ordinary historical evidence

sub_claims.claim: Göbekli Tepe exists as an archaeological site in southeastern Turkey
The site dates to the pre-pottery Neolithic (~9,600–8,000 BCE)
The exact original purpose of the site is fully settled
It is unusually monumental for hunter-gatherer societies of that period

topics.layer_summary: Site existence and age: established. Original purpose: genuinely unresolved · this is one of the interesting open questions in Neolithic archaeology.
topics.discussion_opener: Göbekli Tepe is one of the strongest current examples of a genuinely unresolved archaeological question · not speculation, not consensus.
topics.offer_to_expand: I can walk through what is established about the site and where the main scholarly interpretations diverge.
never_says: the purpose of Göbekli Tepe is definitely known
